selection: All newly discovered matching records in this collection; no fixed paper-count quota.

papers.title: T-cell clonality and TCR repertoire dynamics during germinal center responses: A comprehensive review of regulatory mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities.
papers.authors: Sirati Moghaddam P, Mirzajani Sarvandani M.
papers.abstract: T-cell receptors (TCRs) are pivotal for antigen recognition within germinal centers (GCs), which are essential for B-cell maturation and high-affinity antibody production. Although the role played by T follicular helper (Tfh) cells in supporting B cells is established, the mechanisms driving the expansion and maintenance of distinct T-cell clonotypes in the GC perifollicular region remain poorly understood. This review aims to synthesize current knowledge on the differentiation, migration, and clonal expansion of T cells within GCs, with emphasis on Tfh-B-cell interactions. Findings from immunohistochemistry, flow cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, multiphoton microscopy, and CRISPR/Cas9-based approaches indicate that clonal expansion of T cells carrying defined TCR clonotypes is a regulated process driven by cognate Tfh-B-cell interactions. These interactions promote both B-cell affinity maturation and the concomitant selection and clonal expansion of T cells. The reviewed studies reveal that the TCR repertoire within the GC perifollicular region is refined over time, contributing to the development of long-lived memory and effector cells. The collective results underscore a dynamic reciprocity where T cells shape the antibody response while themselves undergoing antigen-driven selection. Key challenges include clarifying TCR signaling networks, improving in vivo analysis of cellular interactions, and identifying strategies to therapeutically modulate these processes without disrupting immune homeostasis. Overcoming these hurdles will require interdisciplinary approaches and the application of emerging technologies. Future research focused on these areas will be critical for advancing fundamental immunology and developing novel therapeutic strategies for vaccines, autoimmune diseases, and cancer.

papers.title: Plasma proteins and antibody immune responses in non-small cell lung cancer: Evidence from Mendelian randomization, mediation analysis, and single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.authors: Wu L, Feng H, Chai L, Luo X, Zhao C, Wang Y.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo investigate the potential causal relationships between circulating plasma proteins and non-small cell lung cancer and to assess whether antibody immune response traits mediate these associations.MethodsWe conducted an integrative genetic epidemiology study combining two-sample Mendelian randomization, mediation analysis, single-cell transcriptomics, and tissue-based experimental validation. Plasma protein data for 4907 proteins and genome-wide association study summary statistics for 46 antibody immune response traits were analyzed alongside non-small cell lung cancer genome-wide association study data from 218,792 individuals of European ancestry (1627 cases and 217,165 controls). Five complementary Mendelian randomization methods were applied; sensitivity analyses assessed heterogeneity, horizontal pleiotropy, and robustness, and reverse Mendelian randomization assessed potential reverse causation. Mediation analysis evaluated antibody immune response traits as candidate intermediate phenotypes. Prioritized proteins were further characterized using single-cell RNA sequencing data and paired tumor and adjacent normal tissues from patients with histopathologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer.ResultsWe identified 1188 plasma proteins with potential causal associations with non-small cell lung cancer risk. CLEC10A and TGM3 were prioritized through sequential plasma protein-non-small cell lung cancer, plasma protein-antibody immune response, and mediation analyses. Higher genetically predicted CLEC10A levels were associated with increased non-small cell lung cancer risk, whereas higher genetically predicted TGM3 levels were associated with lower non-small cell lung cancer risk. Five antibody immune response traits were initially associated with non-small cell lung cancer, of which four were retained after robustness assessment. Mediation analysis identified three candidate plasma protein-antibody immune response-non-small cell lung cancer pathways involving GCST90006921 and GCST90006923. Single-cell analysis localized CLEC10A and TGM3 predominantly to macrophages, while paired tissue analyses showed higher CLEC10A and lower TGM3 expression in tumors.ConclusionsCLEC10A and TGM3 may contribute to non-small cell lung cancer susceptibility, with specific antibody immune response traits representing candidate intermediate immune pathways. These findings provide genetic and complementary biological support for further independent replication and mechanistic investigation.
papers.venue: The Journal of international medical research

papers.title: Macaque Vγ4+ γδ T cells exhibit distinct IFN-γ and IL-22 effector profiles that are dysregulated during chronic SIV infection and diarrheal disease
papers.authors: McNally, A. B.; Rahmberg, A. R.; Markowitz, T. E.; Hart, V. A.; Do, J.; Thirugnanam, S.; Fukazawa, Y.; Batada, N.; Brenchley, J. M.; Rout, N.
papers.abstract: V{gamma}4+ {gamma}{delta} T cells contribute to colonic homeostasis in humans, but their biology in nonhuman primates remains poorly defined. Here, we characterized V{gamma}4+ {gamma}{delta} T cells in blood and intestinal tissues of healthy, diarrhea-inflicted, and SIV-infected rhesus macaques. TRG/TRD repertoire sequencing across colon, mesenteric lymph node, blood, and spleen revealed compartment-specific clonal architecture and colonic enrichment of TRGV3. Flow cytometric profiling revealed circulating and colonic V{gamma}4+ T cells were predominantly V{delta}1+, exhibited an effector memory phenotype, and displayed T-bet-dominant transcriptional profiles. High-dimensional clustering confirmed V{gamma}4+V{delta}1+ T cells as a distinct terminally differentiated lineage. Functionally, stimulated V{gamma}4+ T cells exhibited robust Th1/Th17 cytokine production, supporting dual inflammatory and barrier-protective roles. Campylobacter-associated diarrhea was characterized by mucosal expansion of central memory V{gamma}4+ T cells and altered cytokine responses. In contrast, ART-suppressed chronic SIV infection was associated with colonic enrichment of naive-like V{gamma}4+ T cells and increased ROR{gamma}t expression, alongside profound systemic loss of cytokine production but relative preservation of mucosal Th17-type responses. Both conditions exhibited a convergent loss of systemic Type 1 effector V{gamma}4+ T-cell responses, pointing to a shared functional alteration during chronic intestinal inflammation. Overall, these findings reveal disease-specific remodeling of V{gamma}4+ T cells during chronic intestinal inflammation and gut barrier disruption in chronic enterocolitis and SIV infection.

papers.title: An APOA5-Derived Signature Bridges Cholesterol Homeostasis to T-Cell Exhaustion and Directs Lung Adenocarcinoma Immunotherapy Response.
papers.authors: Deng M, Su SM, Zhai Z, An T, Wang Y, Yang Y, Mu D, Wang Y, Tang D, Zhang X, Li X, Leung EL, Xu X, Huang C, Deng C.
papers.abstract: Immune heterogeneity and metabolic remodeling frequently limit the efficacy of immunotherapy in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). To address this challenge, we integrated single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing analyses, pairing machine learning with preclinical models to develop the APOA5-correlated T-cell Signature (ACTsig), which effectively stratifies LUAD patients and predicts immunotherapeutic response. Moreover, We identified apolipoprotein A-V (APOA5) as a previously unrecognized tumor suppressor linking cholesterol homeostasis to the tumor immune ecosystem. Mechanistically, APOA5 deficiency induced intracellular cholesterol accumulation and MIF production. Cholesterol depletion and replenishment established a causal role for cholesterol accumulation in regulating MIF production, while MIF knockdown reversed APOA5-loss-induced T-cell exhaustion and recombinant MIF restored the phenotype. Meanwhile, CXCR4 blockade rescued APOA5-loss-induced T-cell exhaustion, supporting the functional involvement of the MIF receptor CXCR4 in this immunosuppressive phenotype. Finally, in silico drug screening identified fenofibrate, which, in combination with anti-PD-1 therapy, significantly suppressed tumor growth in APOA5-deficient models. Together, these findings establish ACTsig as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy response and reveal an APOA5-cholesterol-MIF-CXCR4 axis underlying T-cell exhaustion.

papers.title: Macrophage Immunometabolic Reprogramming in Multiple Myeloma: Linking Spatial Niches to Therapy Resistance.
papers.authors: Wu B, Zhou W, Wu W.
papers.abstract: Background Macrophages in the multiple myeloma (MM) microenvironment adopt diverse functional states that extend beyond the M1/M2 framework. This review examines how spatial niches and metabolic reprogramming shape macrophage function and contribute to therapy resistance. Methods We synthesized published mechanistic, single-cell, and spatial profiling studies, focusing on glycolytic, lipid, amino acid, and mitochondrial pathways across hypoxic, vascular, osteolytic, and extramedullary niches. Results The reviewed evidence suggests that tumor-derived signals, extracellular vesicles, and local metabolic conditions jointly shape macrophage states that can promote immune dysfunction, disease progression, and therapy resistance. Single-cell and spatial profiling studies link macrophage states to cellular neighborhoods, anatomical location, and metabolic context. Conclusions Targeting macrophage signaling, metabolism, phagocytic checkpoints, and niche-specific pathways may help overcome therapy resistance in MM. Most supporting evidence comes from preclinical and in vitro studies, and these strategies require clinical validation.

papers.title: Multimodal Nanohybrid Artificial Antibodies as PD-L1 Immune Checkpoint Antagonists for Potentiated Combination Cancer Immunotherapy.
papers.authors: Lee S, Choi Y, So Y, Yu Y, Choi C, Kim H, Moon S, Choi S, Lee H, Kim JH.
papers.abstract: Monoclonal antibody-based PD-1/PD-L1 blockade immunotherapy is an innovative approach to cancer treatment. However, its clinical efficacy remains limited, with low response rates in patients, requiring multimodal therapeutic approaches. This study reports the development of synthetic nanohybrid artificial antibodies (SNA) with both PD-L1 blockade and photothermal effects as multimodal immune checkpoint antagonists for effective combination cancer immunotherapy. Multimodal SNAs are prepared by assembling multivalent tripeptide recognition phases onto rigid scaffolds of WS 2 or MoSe 2 nanosheets with photothermal effect. The SNAs, comprising an FNP tripeptide assembly on nanosheets (MoSe 2 -FNP & WS 2 -FNP), selectively bind to PD-L1 with sub-nanomolar apparent affinity (0.785 nM), thereby effectively blocking its interaction with PD-1 on T cells. Thorough experimental and computational results reveal that the recognition selectivity of the SNAs for PD-L1 is attributed to their multivalent hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions with the PD-L1 epitope. The multimodal MoSe 2 -FNP more effectively eradicates tumor cells by combining a PD-L1 blockade with photothermal effect. The multimodal MoSe 2 -FNP-based combination immunotherapy accelerates the infiltration of antitumoral immune cells into solid tumors in mice, and its therapeutic efficacy is significantly enhanced compared with monoclonal antibody treatment. This SNA-based cancer immunotherapy thus holds considerable promise as an effective therapeutic avenue for cancer treatment.

papers.title: Unfolded protein response and senescence associated transcriptional programs define prognostic heterogeneity and malignant cell states in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.authors: Xiong T, Peng W, Yi J, Chen Z, Zhu H, Tang L, Mao J, Qiu Y, Yan J, Hu Z, Wang K.
papers.abstract: The unfolded protein response (UPR) and senescence-associated transcriptional programs are implicated in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but their relationships with tumor heterogeneity, prognosis, and the immune microenvironment remain unclear. We integrated bulk and single cell transcriptomic analyses with experimental assays. Bulk transcriptomic clustering identified four molecular subtypes, including C3, which showed enrichment of selected UPR, senescence, and cell cycle-associated signatures and was associated with poor prognosis. We developed a UPR and senescence related score (USRS) from C3-associated prognostic genes. USRS was associated with overall survival across multiple cohorts and remained prognostically informative after adjustment for clinical variables. Single cell analysis identified MalC3, a malignant cell subcluster exhibiting some transcriptional features resembling those of bulk C3. To explore regulatory features of this subcluster, network analysis prioritized Yin Yang 1 (YY1) as a candidate upstream regulator of activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4). Dual luciferase assays supported YY1 dependent regulation of ATF4 promoter activity. In parallel, cell-cell communication analysis predicted a potential interaction between tumor-cell apolipoprotein E (APOE) and macrophage triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2). Multiplex immunofluorescence revealed spatial proximity between APOE-positive tumor cells and TREM2-positive macrophages in hepatocellular carcinoma tissues, with PD-L1 expression observed in the surrounding regions, suggesting a potential association with an immunosuppression-related tumor microenvironment. Together, these findings delineate prognostically relevant transcriptional heterogeneity in HCC and identify potential regulatory and tumor-macrophage communication relationships for further study.

papers.title: Golgi-retained TNFR1 variants induce stress-driven inflammation in a subset of systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
papers.authors: Cruz AC, Csomos K, Nakano H, Ujhazi B, Panipinto PM, Chou SR, Krantz M, Rosenbaum ED, Correia Marques M, Felicelli C, Fu TM, Foell D, Yeung RS, Weiss PF, Naz F, Bergeron LL, Millwood M, Lake C, Nagao K, Schaughency P, Chen V, Lack J, Verweyen EL, Schulert G, Yu K, INCHARGE Consortium, Dell'Orso S, Wu H, Deng Z, Randazzo D, Ombrello MJ.
papers.abstract: Systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA) is a complex inflammatory disease characterized by recurrent fevers, arthritis, and systemic hyperinflammation; however, its underlying etiology remains poorly understood. Tumor necrosis factor receptor 1 (TNFR1, TNFRSF1A), the prototypical TNF superfamily receptor, signals through its ligand (tumor necrosis factor, TNF) to activate NF-κB-dependent proinflammatory pathways while also promoting cell death. Through family-based and targeted sequencing, we identified multiple rare TNFRSF1A variants, including a de novo truncating variant in a patient with monophasic sJIA. Integrating single cell RNA-seq with in vitro and ex vivo functional assays, we uncovered a patient-specific, unique monocyte population marked by high inflammatory cytokine production. These cells display impaired endosomal and Golgi trafficking, dysregulated autophagy, and increased markers of cellular stress and immune activation. Confocal microscopy revealed aberrant TNFR1 retention within the Golgi apparatus. These monocytes were refractory to LPS-induced cell death, maintained a M1-like inflammatory phenotype and produced proinflammatory cytokines even at steady state. Despite conferring a loss of function in TNFR1 signaling, these variants paradoxically drive a hyperinflammatory phenotype. We propose that this results from combined effects of reduced TNFR1 signaling and cellular stress induced by retention of the mutant receptor in the Golgi.

papers.title: Hypofractionated Radiotherapy Elicits Tumor-Derived APOC2 to Drive Inflammatory Monocyte Differentiation and Potentiate Anti-Tumor Immunity in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.authors: Xu Q, Wang H, Li M, Zou Z, Liu L, Zheng L, Kang D, Sun R, Cheng C, Xu K, Ren J, Zhang L, Han C, Zhang P, Tao K, Lin Z, Zhang T.
papers.abstract: Hypofractionated radiotherapy (HFRT) combined with immunochemotherapy holds promise for overcoming immune resistance in microsatellite-stable (MSS) locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). However, the mechanisms underlying its effects remain unclear. Using secretome profiling, ATAC-seq, bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, we investigated how HFRT remodels the tumor immune microenvironment. APOC2 was induced by HFRT, and higher post-treatment serum APOC2 levels were associated with pathologic complete response (pCR) to HFRT-based neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy. Mechanistically, HFRT reduced ATF3 expression, relieving its repression of the APOC2 promoter and increasing tumor-cell APOC2 secretion. APOC2 activated lipoprotein lipase, increased free fatty acid production, enhanced type I interferon signaling, and promoted the differentiation of Ly6A + inflammatory monocytes. These monocytes exhibit specialized MHC class I antigen-presentation programs that bolster CD8 + T-cell effector functions. Clinically, the APOC2 nomogram demonstrated consistent discriminative ability for pCR across the discovery and internal validation cohorts. Therapeutic supplementation with recombinant APOC2 or APOC2-loaded nanoliposomes (APOC2@NL) sensitized murine tumors to HFRT plus PD-1 blockade. These findings position APOC2 as a functional mediator between radiotherapy-induced metabolism and antitumor immunity, offering a promising biomarker and a preclinical therapeutic proof of concept for LARC.

papers.title: Tumo​r-associated macrophages in ovarian, prostate, thyroid and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors: molecular crosstalk and therapeutic perspectives.
papers.authors: Patel D, Ravindran S, Sojan MM, Suresh PS.
papers.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are key regulators of the tumor microenvironment and play dual roles in endocrine cancer progression by exhibiting remarkable functional plasticity beyond the conventional M1/M2 paradigm. Their interactions with tumor cells influence immune evasion, angiogenesis, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance through complex signaling networks and extracellular vesicle-mediated communication. This review summarizes the current understanding of TAM biology across some key endocrine and hormone-dependent cancers, including ovarian, prostate, thyroid, and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, highlighting their prognostic significance and molecular mechanisms. We further discuss emerging TAM-targeted therapeutic strategies, including macrophage depletion, immune checkpoint modulation, macrophage reprogramming, and nanoparticle-based approaches. Finally, we outline the challenges associated with clinical translation and emphasize the potential of single-cell and multi-omics technologies to enable precision macrophage-targeted therapies for endocrine cancers, including a summary of recent developments in the field of precision mapping of TAMs.

papers.title: Oroxylin A attenuates pneumonia via HSP90α-dependent suppression of macrophage ferroptosis-mediated inflammation.
papers.authors: Xing X, Jiang Y, Wang J, Li X, Zhang Q, Zhao P, Du Y, Mei X.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the protective activity of Oroxylin A in pneumonia and to clarify the mechanisms involved, particularly those associated with macrophage-driven inflammation and ferroptosis. Pneumonia was induced in mice and treated with Oroxylin A, followed by evaluation of lung injury, inflammatory cytokine production, and ferroptosis-related markers. Pulmonary immune alterations were further characterized by single-cell RNA sequencing. Target-responsive accessibility profiling, molecular dynamics simulation, and cellular thermal shift assays were subsequently applied to explore potential molecular targets, followed by functional verification in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-challenged macrophages. Oroxylin A alleviated body weight loss, pathological lung injury, alveolar inflammation, and inflammatory cytokine production in mice with pneumonia. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis identified macrophages as a major responsive population and showed that Oroxylin A modulated inflammation- and ferroptosis-related transcriptional programs. In LPS-stimulated macrophages, Oroxylin A suppressed the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and increased GPX4 and SLC7A11 expression, whereas these effects were attenuated by erastin. Heat shock protein 90-alpha (HSP90α) was further identified as a potential binding target of Oroxylin A. In silico perturbation analyses suggested that HSP90α participates in ferroptosis-related biological processes. Functional experiments showed that HSP90α overexpression weakened the anti-inflammatory and anti-ferroptotic actions of Oroxylin A, whereas HSP90α knockdown suppressed inflammatory cytokine expression and increased GPX4 expression. Collectively, these findings suggest that Oroxylin A alleviates pneumonia-associated inflammation through an HSP90α-dependent mechanism involving the regulation of macrophage ferroptosis.

papers.title: Targeting Protein Tyrosine Phosphatases in Cancer: Dual Roles and Therapeutic Implications.
papers.authors: Cao J, Peng S, Lin X, Jing J, Ma L.
papers.abstract: Protein Tyrosine Phosphatases (PTPs) play a dual role in cancer as both tumor suppressors and oncogenic drivers by dephosphorylating key signaling molecules. They take part in core oncogenic pathways, either suppressing tumor formation or promoting cancer progression through proliferation and immune suppression. Recent therapeutic advances have explored allosteric inhibitors, degraders and combination approaches targeting non-catalytic regulatory domains or the ubiquitin-proteasome system. Combined with immune checkpoint blockade, these strategies have potential to resolve selectivity limitations of traditional catalytic-site inhibitors alongside hard-to-target and dual-role challenges. This paper proposes a paradigm shift from single enzyme activity inhibition to microenvironment regulation and combination strategies, emphasizing the need to target non-catalytic regions and integrate the Tumor Microenvironment (TME) using single-cell spatial transcriptomics and biomarker analysis to advance combinations of PTP inhibitors and immune checkpoint inhibitors from preclinical models toward early-phase clinical investigation. METHOD: We conducted a narrative review of PubMed through October 2026 and hand-searched reference lists of relevant guidelines, reviews, and primary studies. We prioritized international guidance, systematic reviews, multicenter registries, prospective cohorts, and clinically informative mechanistic studies. Case reports and experimental studies were kept when they addressed questions not covered by higher-level evidence. The review was not protocol driven and did not include duplicate screening, formal risk-of-bias assessment, or a PRISMA flow diagram.

papers.title: A prognostic model based on platelet-related genes accurately predicts survival in patients with gastric cancer.
papers.authors: Zheng C, Yang W, Lu Q, Zhou Y.
papers.abstract: Background Platelets contribute to gastric cancer (GC) progression and metastasis. In this study, we aimed to construct a prognostic model based on platelet-related genes (PRGs) to predict outcomes in GC. Methods RNA sequencing data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes, from which PRGs were selected as candidates. A prognostic model was built using machine learning. Immune infiltration was evaluated with CIBERSORT, and Spearman correlation was used to assess the relationships between prognostic PRGs and immune cells. Single-cell transcriptomics was used to explore cellular expression patterns, and molecular regulatory networks were constructed. The expression of candidate genes was validated in cell lines by reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Results A total of 8,387 differentially expressed genes, including 123 PRGs, were identified. An eight-gene prognostic model (THPO, MMRN1, EGF, SPARC, GNAI1, CD36, SERPINE1, and ADAMTS18) was established. Distinct immune infiltration patterns were observed between risk groups, with differences in M2 macrophages, monocytes, neutrophils, activated memory CD4+ T cells, regulatory T cells, and follicular helper T cells. MMRN1 expression correlated positively with monocytes ( r = 0.37), whereas GNAI1 expression was negatively associated with activated memory CD4+ T cells ( r = - 0.30). Single-cell analysis showed that prognostic genes were mainly expressed in epithelial cells and fibroblasts. Two regulatory axes, SPARC-hsa-miR-494-3p-NEAT1 and GNAI1-hsa-miR-4262-NEAT1, were implicated in GC progression. RT-qPCR confirmed downregulation of CD36 and upregulation of SERPINE1 in GC tissues. Conclusion This platelet-related gene model predicts survival and immune infiltration in GC and may support the development of personalized therapies.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese Medicine for Hepatocellular Carcinoma: An Evidence-Mapped Narrative Review of Clinical Certainty, Mechanisms, and Translational Gaps.
papers.authors: He H, Wang J, Huang J, Zhang X.
papers.abstract: This evidence-mapped narrative review evaluates traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) across clinical, preclinical, computational, and theoretical evidence. The original search cutoff was June 2026, and the evidence map comprised 139 bibliographic records, originally distributed between 89 main-text references and 50 supplementary records. Targeted literature verification during revision supplemented this map with treatment benchmarks and relevant clinical studies. Certainty judgments are preliminary narrative assessments, not formal outcome-level GRADE ratings. TACE plus Chinese herbal medicine and selected standardized preparations show the most consistent, low-to-moderate preliminary clinical signal, mainly for short-term tumor response and quality-of-life-related outcomes. Individual survival-endpoint trials, including an Rg3-TACE trial and a multicenter postoperative Huaier trial, warrant separate consideration and do not establish a class-wide survival benefit. Clinical reports of TCM plus targeted agents exist, but their methodological limitations prevent firm conclusions. No prospective clinical efficacy evidence for TCM combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors was identified in this review. Mechanistic studies support hypotheses involving cell death, the tumor microenvironment, and the gut-liver axis; heterogeneous models and limited causal or exposure validation constrain translation. Postoperative prevention, palliative care, and pattern-based prescribing remain incompletely supported. Priorities are reproducible searches, product-specific multicenter trials with survival or validated patient-reported endpoints, pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic characterization, nutritional assessment, and staged safety evaluation before immunotherapy combination trials.

papers.title: Immune interaction signatures in adipose tissue fibroblasts in obesity-associated atherosclerosis.
papers.authors: Lea M, Aydin B, Minna P, Ivana M, Mira V, Jimmy F, Harri H, Antti S, de Sande Ana H, Senthil P, Tiit Ö, Anne R, Pekka R, Merja H, Minna KU, Tapio L.
papers.abstract: Atherosclerosis involves changes in the vascular wall and surrounding perivascular adipose tissue, yet the cellular contributors to disease progression remain incompletely understood. Obesity exacerbates atherogenesis, but the cell types driving this aggravation are unclear. We aimed to define the key cell populations across tissues in a highly atherogenic mouse model under obese and normal-weight conditions and to identify obesity-associated cellular changes. We employed 5' single-cell RNA sequencing combined with antibody staining in Ldlr -/- Apob 100/100 male mice fed either a high-fat or control diet. Aorta, perivascular and epididymal adipose tissues, and spleen were analyzed, with CD45 + enrichment of aortic samples and CITE-seq using a 138-antibody panel. Key findings were validated in mice by immunohistochemistry and multiplexed immunofluorescence and explored in human aorta and carotid arteries using spatial transcriptomics. Analysis of ∼46,000 cells enabled characterization of cell states, gene enrichment, regulon activity, and inferred interactions. Adipose-derived fibroblast subsets displayed immune-associated transcriptional programs in obesity. The frequency of PI16 + progenitor fibroblasts was reduced per unit area, alongside marked PVAT remodelling, and the top mouse differentially expressed genes exhibited clear spatial patterning in human arteries.

papers.title: CD8a-Functionalized Red Blood Cell Membrane Nanovesicles Delivering KRN2 for Coordinated T Cell Reinvigoration and Macrophage Metabolic Reprogramming in Cardia Cancer.
papers.authors: Zhang X, Xiang Z, Wang W, Cao H, Song H, You W, Guo C, Wang A, Zhang B, Jia J.
papers.abstract: Engineered biomimetic nanovesicle systems represent an emerging strategy for targeted immune modulation in cancer. In this study, we developed anti-CD8a-functionalized red blood cell membrane-derived nanovesicles (NVE) to selectively deliver the NFAT5 inhibitor KRN2 to CD8 + T cells. Transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing analyses identified NFAT5 as a transcriptional regulator associated with PD-1 expression in highly exhausted CD8 + T cell subsets in cardia cancer. CD8a-NVE@KRN2 showed favourable physicochemical properties, efficient KRN2 loading, and preferential CD8 + T cell targeting. Functionally, targeted NFAT5 inhibition restored CD8 + T cell activity, promoted granzyme A-gasdermin B-mediated tumour cell pyroptosis, and indirectly shifted tumour-associated macrophages toward a more inflammatory, glycolysis-associated phenotype. In subcutaneous and orthotopic models, CD8a-NVE@KRN2 enhanced the antitumour effect of anti-PD-1 therapy. These findings support functionalized red blood cell membrane nanovesicles as a biomimetic platform for coordinated immune reprogramming in cancer.

papers.title: Multidimensional Deciphering Underlying Effects of PFOA Exposure in Ulcerative Colitis: From Epidemiological Insights to Toxicological Mechanisms.
papers.authors: Zhang H, Liu Y, Zhao Y, Li W, Han Y, Liu J, Wang H, Wang Z, He Z, Bai Y.
papers.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a representative persistent organic pollutant (POP), has been linked to numerous adverse health effects. Ulcerative colitis (UC), characterized by recurrent colon inflammation, is known to have environmental exposure as a primary etiological factor; however, the toxicological mechanisms underlying PFOA-induced UC remain unclear. This study therefore aims to comprehensively investigate the association between PFOA exposure and UC. A meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate the association between PFOA exposure and UC onset, and network toxicology, cross-species transcriptomics, protein-protein interaction networks, and weighted gene coexpression network analysis were employed to identify potential targets and mechanisms. Single-cell RNA sequencing, molecular docking, and Mendelian randomization were used to pinpoint and validate hub genes, while in vivo DSS-induced colitis and in vitro inflammation models were applied to assess the functional impact of PFOA. The meta-analysis of four studies confirmed a significant positive association between PFOA exposure and UC risk (Fisher z = 0.20, 95% CI: 0.13-0.27). We identified 170 overlapping targets linking PFOA to UC, predominantly enriched in immune-inflammatory activation and metabolic disruption. Seven hub genes (IRF1, CXCL1, CXCL9, CXCL10, CXCL11, CASP1, and IL1B) constituted a UC-associated coexpression module, with monocytes/macrophages as primary sources by single-cell profiling. Molecular docking confirmed PFOA binding to these proteins, and Mendelian randomization established IRF1 as a causal risk factor. In vivo, PFOA exacerbated DSS-induced colitis, impairing barrier function, promoting apoptosis and mitochondrial dysfunction. In conclusion, PFOA exposure is associated with increased UC risk and may promote colonic inflammation by affecting the chemokine-inflammasome network and epithelial function. IRF1 may be a key hub in this process, but its upstream role needs validation. These findings highlight the potential importance of reducing environmental pollutant exposure in UC prevention.

papers.title: Isolation and characterization of human thymic epithelial cells.
papers.authors: Lin Y, Lapine ME, Netz DM, Chapin SR, K Prabakar R, Meyer HV.
papers.abstract: The human thymus is critical for establishing a functional adaptive immune system, with reduced cancer risk, increased healthy aging, and longevity all linked to its function. However, the molecular and physiological mechanisms of these associations are incompletely understood. For the reproducible identification of mechanisms and mitigating cell types, consistent tissue processing and analysis techniques are essential. Here, we assessed biological and technical parameters for the processing, isolation, and analyses of human thymic epithelial cells (TECs). We found that EpCAM and autofluorescence emissions in the range of 500 to 650 nm excited by the 405 nm laser are sufficient to distinguish TECs from other thymic cells, particularly the autofluorescent population. We identified CD205 as the target of the classical cortical TEC antibody CDR2 and re-established CD205 as a reliable marker to distinguish cortical and medullary TECs, which we confirmed by single-cell RNA sequencing. In a systematic comparison of sample processing and digestion conditions, we assessed representative tissue sample size and protein staining patterns, which enabled us to clarify and reconcile inconsistencies across previously published results. Lastly, we established a minimal flow cytometry panel sequencing for the isolation of major TEC populations and their developmental stages. In summary, we provide recommendations to improve reproducibility in the study of human TEC biology and thymus function.

papers.title: Synthetic Dental Carries Vaccine Design Study: Fragile Alpha Helix From the Stalk of Streptococcus mutans and Streptococcus sobrinus Major Adhesins.
papers.authors: Khrustalev VV, Khrustaleva OV, Maliushkova EV, Semak IV, Tarasik MS, Matusevich PV, Kharytonova UV, Rubnikovich SP, Miskevich OE, Stojarov AN.
papers.abstract: Dental carries can be prevented by neutralizing IgA and IgG antibodies against Streptococci inhabiting the oral cavity. Epitopes for neutralizing antibodies against Streptococcus mutans and Streptococcus sobrinus are situated along the surface of their major adhesins. The stalk of such adhesin is represented by the long Ala-rich alpha helix intertwining with Pro-rich sequence. The aim of this study was to select a synthetic antigen from the major adhesin of S. mutans or S. sobrinus with the same conformation as in the fragment of the full-length protein. Initial bioinformatics steps of vaccine peptide design included secondary structure stability assessment and molecular dynamics simulations. Eight antigens from the most stable part of the stalk of the major adhesin have been synthetized and tested by ATR-IR spectroscopy, CD spectroscopy, BN PAGE, SDS PAGE, and fluorescence spectroscopy. According to CD-spectroscopy, both the Ala-rich fragment of the stalk of the major adhesin of S. mutans (NEADYQAKLTAYQTELAR) and S. sobrinus (NEADYQEKLAAYEKELAR) alone and in combination with the Pro-rich fragment (EKEPTPPTRTPD and EKEPTPPSKTPD, consequently) are prone to form beta structure in a completely hydrated state even if they are conjugated with BSA. However, according to ATR-IR spectroscopy on both hydrophobic and hydrophilic surfaces, in a partially dehydrated state the peptide with the NEADYQEKLAAYEKELARGPPGEKEPTPPSKTPD sequence can turn to alpha-helical conformation. These facts are explained by the presence of hydrophobic and hydrophilic amino acid residues interpolations characteristic to beta structure in sequences enriched by residues prone to form alpha helices. Further modifications of the most promising peptide and its conjugation with other carriers is the new pathway for future carries vaccine development.

papers.title: Immune-stimulatory cytokine IL-18 induces inflammatory senescence and impairs stem cell-mediated experimental skeletal regeneration.
papers.authors: Gao Y, Wang L, Gan Y, Lin Q, Chen S, Li M, Chen J, Shen H, Zheng Q, Sokolowskei D, Tower RJ, Huang M, Xu J, James AW, Bai X, Zhang Z, Xu J.
papers.abstract: Stem cell-based therapies offer potential for repairing large skeletal defects, yet persistent inflammation limits their efficacy. Here, we identify macrophage-derived IL-18 as an immune switch that impairs skeletal regeneration by disrupting immune-mesenchymal cell interactions. IL-18 is elevated in male mouse non-healing models and human bone nonunion samples, supporting its translational relevance. Mechanistically, IL-18 acts as an upstream amplifier of inflammation by inducing Serpina3f transcription, thereby driving macrophage senescence and M1 polarization and triggering a feed-forward inflammatory cascade that suppresses mesenchymal stem/stromal cell osteogenesis. Single-cell RNA sequencing and functional assays further show that IL-18 directly impairs mesenchymal stem/stromal cell proliferation, clonogenicity, and mitochondrial fitness. Genetic deletion of IL-18 restores regenerative potential, whereas pharmacological blockade with IL-18-neutralizing antibodies or IL-18 binding protein reverses macrophage dysfunction and promotes bone healing. These findings establish IL-18 as a key mediator of inflammation-induced regenerative failure and a potential therapeutic target for skeletal regeneration.
